paper.title_en: Explaining the \(B\rightarrow K\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\) anomaly in the left-right inverse seesaw model
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the long-standing anomaly in the rare decay <math display="inline"><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>K</mi><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math> within the left-right inverse seesaw (LRIS) model. Global analyses of the <math display="inline"><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>s</mi><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math> data consistently indicate a significant negative shift in the vector Wilson coefficient, <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mn>9</mn><mi>μ</mi></msubsup><mo>≈</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, while the axial coefficient <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mn>10</mn><mi>μ</mi></msubsup></math> remains consistent with zero. We show that a charged-scalar/heavy-neutrino box diagram in the LRIS model naturally generates these values for the Wilson coefficients through a nondecoupling mechanism: the right-handed coupling <math display="inline"><msubsup><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow><mi>R</mi></msubsup><mo>∝</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></math> produces a contribution to <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mn>9</mn><mi>μ</mi></msubsup></math> that is unsuppressed in the heavy-neutrino limit, while the simultaneous presence of a comparable left-handed Dirac Yukawa coupling <math display="inline"><msubsup><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup></math> ensures the automatic cancellation <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mn>10</mn><mi>μ</mi></msubsup><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. The potentially dangerous contribution to <math display="inline"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></math> mixing is controlled by the usual Glashow–Iliopoulos–Maiani suppression associated with the top-quark loop, keeping it safely below current experimental bounds throughout the viable parameter space. In addition, a specific right-handed phase texture in the right-handed quark mixing matrix, whose origin can be traced to a discrete <math display="inline"><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> symmetry in the right-handed quark sector, provides a technically natural and radiatively stable structural feature of the model. A numerical scan over the model parameter space identifies a viable region with <math display="inline"><mi>y</mi><mo>≡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow><mi>H</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.39</mn></math> and <math display="inline"><msub><mi>M</mi><msup><mi>H</mi><mo>±</mo></msup></msub><mo>≳</mo><mn>600</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>GeV</mi></math>, consistent with current flavor and collider experimental constraints.
